diagnosis.root_cause: The ONU is online with healthy optical levels and valid RADIUS authentication, but its customer service VLAN is still set to factory-default VLAN 46 instead of the expected VLAN 1116. This leaves the newly installed subscriber without service.
evidence: The ONU is currently online and responds successfully; it reports Auth and Finish.
RX power is -18.95 dBm and TX power is 2.51 dBm, both within the healthy EPON ranges.
The seven-day optical telemetry is stable: RX remains around -19 dBm, TX around +2.3 dBm, distance is constant at 52, and TX bias remains healthy without a rising trend.
All probed peers on EPON0/6 are online, so there is no evidence of an ONU, splitter, PON-port, or shared OLT fault.
The OLT and router are healthy and reachable, with normal CPU, memory, temperature, and heartbeat values.
The RADIUS entry exists, the line ID matches CRM, and there are no authentication mismatches.
There are zero sessions and zero traffic because the service VLAN walk shows actual VLAN 46 while customer VLAN 1116 is expected.
VLAN 46 is explicitly the factory-default, never-provisioned VLAN, matching the complaint that installation completed two days ago but service never started.

remediation.action: Complete provisioning for the subscriber by replacing VLAN 46 with customer VLAN 1116 on the ONU/service path, then verify DHCP/IP assignment, RADIUS session establishment, and subscriber traffic. Recheck the ONU configuration after provisioning.

ground_truth.root_cause: The CPE is still on VLAN 46, the factory-default management VLAN it ships with. The TR-069 provisioning step that migrates it to VLAN 1999 and its data VLAN never completed, so the device is registered on the fibre but has no path onto the network.
expected_reasoning: The ONU is online with RX -18.92 and TX 2.50, both excellent
The live probe confirms the ONU and its peers are responding normally
The OLT and router are healthy, so the physical layer works end to end
Despite that, the customer has zero sessions and zero traffic since installation
A radcheck row does exist for this CPE MAC, so this is not a missing RADIUS entry
The VLAN walk shows the customer on VLAN 46 where VLAN 1116 is expected
VLAN 46 is the factory-default management VLAN a CPE ships with
Provisioning should have migrated it to 1999 and the port's data VLAN, and did not
The device is present on the fibre and has no path onto the network
distractors: Zero sessions with a healthy physical layer is also the RADIUS missing-entry signature
Excellent optical readings invite a no_fault conclusion on the network side
The VLAN walk is not an obvious first move
